correctness.rationale: Writing y=λt/2, A=λ²exp(-3y), P(y)=1+y+y²/2+y³/6, the normalized hazard is H=(4A+y³/6)/(A+P). Its derivative has numerator proportional to y²F−6AG with F=y²+4y+6 and G=3y³+15y²+32y+32. Thus sign=sign(Q(y)−λ²). The polynomial 3FG+F'G−FG'=9y^5+78y^4+306y³+668y²+844y+512 is positive, establishing Q'/Q>2/y; hence Q rises bijectively and t(y)=2y/sqrt(Q(y)) strictly decreases. Series inversion Q(y)=y²/32+y³/12+O(y⁴) gives 8sqrt2−256λ/3+O(λ²); Q~y exp(3y)/18 gives log correction. Independently evaluated derivative, symbolic series inversion, and sign checks. The rate, time normalization, λ>0 and endpoint domains match the proof.
residual_risks: Computational samples are finite and do not independently certify unquantified infinite-domain conditions.
